feedback.details: Mermaid diagram passes mmdc validation (exit 0) and includes technology labels (Node.js/Express, Python, Markdown/PostgreSQL) and a cross-reference table (c2-container.md:137-158). However, node IDs still do NOT follow the required `id_<SECTION>_<NAME>` format. Current IDs use `id_<short_name>` (e.g., `id_api_gw`, `id_qr_scan`, `id_tg_webhook` at c2-container.md:26-35) instead of `id_EFS_API_GATEWAY`, `id_EFS_QR_SCAN_FUNC`, etc. This was flagged as a recurring concern in Sprint 6 Rounds 1 and 2 (critic-history.md:405, 418) and remains unresolved. The contract explicitly requires node IDs formatted as `id_<SECTION>_<NAME>` — the current format is incomplete.

Comprehensive auth specification in deployment.md. JWT RS256 (line 16), all required claims — iss (line 18), sub (line 19), exp (line 20), scope (line 21), aud (line 22). Token expiration ≤24h (line 20). Refresh strategy with rotation on use (line 35). Environment variables fully specified: JWT_ISSUER, JWT_AUDIENCE, JWT_PUBLIC_KEY, HERMES_ENDPOINT, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (deployment.md:26-32). Threat model subsection (deployment.md:40-50) covers FR36-FR40 prevention with 6 defense layers. Minor gap: the contract states 'JWT RS256 validation via Hermes agent' but the document describes verification against Hermes' public key without detailing how the key is fetched or rotated.

All required parameters present in deployment.md: Kubernetes HPA (line 57), min=1/max=10 replicas (lines 58-59), CPU>70% or memory>80% sustained for 2 minutes (lines 60-62), 5-minute cooldown (line 65), explicit rollback policy on failed scale-up (line 69). Load test k6 configuration (deployment.md:74-102) validates the 50 simultaneous QR scan peak load scenario with proper thresholds. Scale-up/scale-down behavior rates specified (lines 67-68). No significant gaps.

Complete OpenTelemetry-compliant stack (deployment.md:107-199). JSON logging with traceID/correlationID (lines 112-119) with sample entry. /metrics endpoint exposes qr_scans_total and hermes_analysis_latency_seconds (lines 141-146). W3C TraceContext propagation (lines 158-159). Prometheus alert rules YAML for >5% 5xx errors (lines 173-180) and p95>2s latency (lines 182-189). Log retention ≥30 days (line 122). All required elements present with concrete configuration.

feedback.criterion: PRD Accuracy for Edge Function Responsibilities
feedback.details: deployment.md traceability table (lines 203-233) covers FR12-FR21, FR36-FR41, and NFR1-NFR5 with diagram node references. Edge function as data access layer stated (c2-container.md:15-16, 165). Hermes webhook endpoint via HERMES_ENDPOINT env var (deployment.md:31). Plant records markdown storage per FR7-FR11 documented. Anchor cross-links present in c2-container.md relationship table (e.g., [FR12](#fr12-qr-scan-retrieval) at line 139). However, c2-container.md lacks its own structured traceability table — only the relationship description table exists, which maps arrows to PRD refs but does not comprehensively map all FR12-FR15 and FR17-FR21 to exact config keys as required. The traceability in c2-container.md is implicit rather than explicit.

Both files fail catastrophically on markdownlint with the sprint 6 rules (MD009, MD047, MD013 max 100 chars, MD031, MD033 disabled). c2-container.md: 41 errors — 1×MD025, 24×MD022 (blanks around headings), 8×MD060 (table style), 1×MD051 (invalid link fragment), 6×MD013 (line length), 1×MD047. deployment.md: 93 errors — 1×MD025, ~32×MD013 (line length, concentrated in traceability table rows at lines 205-233), 10×MD022, 6×MD032, 2×MD058, 15×MD060, 4×MD009, 2×MD031, 1×MD047. This is a recurring critical failure from Rounds 1 (3.0) and 2 (4.0) — marginally improved but still fundamentally broken. The MD013 violations in deployment.md are driven by the traceability table having extremely long rows (up to 185 characters at line 221). The MD022 violations are systematic — every ### heading lacks a blank line below it. This has been a persistent issue across ALL sprints in critic history.

feedback.criterion: Edge Case: Hermes Agent Fallback Documentation
feedback.details: Comprehensive fallback documentation in deployment.md (lines 235-285). Offline mode specified (line 240): local processing only, plant data without analysis. Queue mechanism: Redis-backed with file-based fallback (line 242), depth limit ≤1000 (line 243), exponential backoff `2^attempt × 1s` capped at 60s (line 244). User notification: Telegram message 'Analysis delayed' (line 245). Idempotency key format: `hermes_req:{plant_id}:{timestamp}:{random_hex}` (line 246). Dead letter queue after 5 attempts (line 247). Sequence diagram for data integrity preservation (FR6-FR11) at lines 250-275. Fallback behavior matrix at lines 279-285. All required elements present.

overall_summary: Sprint 6 Round 3 shows marginal improvement from Round 2 (7.7 average) with no regression in technical depth. Authentication (9.0), Horizontal Scaling (9.0), Observability (9.0), and Hermes Fallback (9.0) remain strong anchors — all four technical criteria are thoroughly specified with concrete parameters, configuration snippets, and YAML examples. However, two persistent blockers prevent contract approval: (1) Markdown Readability & Linting Standards scores 3.5 — both files have 134 total markdownlint errors, driven by systematic MD013 violations in the traceability table (up to 185 chars/line), pervasive MD022 heading-spacing errors, and MD060 table-style violations. This has been a critical failure across every sprint in the critic history. (2) C4 Container Diagram Validity scores 7.0 — node IDs still use the incomplete `id_<short_name>` format instead of the contract-required `id_<SECTION>_<NAME>` format, a recurring issue flagged in Rounds 1 and 2. PRD Accuracy (7.0) is held back because c2-container.md lacks an explicit structured traceability table. The average score of 7.6 falls below the 9.0+ thresholds required by the sprint contract.
